title: How extreme rain is putting orangutans at risk
description:
Orangutans are the world’s most endangered apes and they’re now even closer to extinction. They live on two islands in southeast Asia: Sumatra and Borneo. In November, an extreme weather event in the area killed more than 1,000 people there, plus about 7% of the world’s rarest type of orangutan according to a new study.

BBC Climate and Science reporter Georgina Rannard takes us through how orangutans are being pushed towards extinction and what some countries and charities are doing to protect them.

We also hear from a conservationist making an effort to save the species.

summaryZh: 本 集 探討 紅 毛 猩猩（ orangutan ）面臨 的 風險，牠們 居住 在 印尼 和 馬來西亞 的 Sumatra 及 Borneo 島上。 篇 中 說明 森林 砍伐、 棕櫚油 農場、 採礦、 走私 販售 與 極端 天氣（包括 強降雨 與 颱風）如何 使 稀有 的 Tapanuli 物種 更 接近 滅絕。 節目 也 討論 了 保育 工作， 包括 設立 保護 區、 繁育 計畫 及 富國 支付 弱勢 國家 保持 森林 的 構想，以 期 減緩 物種 滅絕 的 風險。
summaryEn: This episode explains how orangutans on Sumatra and Borneo are threatened by deforestation for palm oil, mining, illegal trafficking, and extreme weather such as heavy rainfall and cyclones. It highlights the particularly dire situation for the Tapanuli orangutan and outlines conservation responses including protected zones, breeding programmes and international payments to keep forests standing.
